root_idea.summary: The root denotes joining or bringing one thing together with another, especially by writing, binding, or assembling.
root_idea.development: From the idea of joining, it develops into writing as the joining of letters, then into a written document, an established prescription or decree, a record, and a formal contract.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Form I verb with distinct Quranic writing, prescribing, and inclusion uses.
Form III verb with the Quranic written-emancipation-contract construction.
Form VIII verb with the Quranic sense of having a text written or fabricated.
Active participle with Quranic writer, recorder, and learned-person uses.
Inflected possessive form كتابي, the same noun as كتاب.
Distinct passive participle مَكْتُوب meaning written or recorded.

senses.usage_conditions: Includes writing down a text, statement, or account; active, passive, and imperative forms occur in the Quran.

senses.definition: To prescribe, ordain, decree, or establish as fixed or due.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for divine laws and obligations, appointed outcomes, allotted matters, and what is firmly established, including something established in the heart. The passive construction كُتِبَ عَلَى or كُتِبَ لِ commonly means “was prescribed” or “was decreed for.”

senses.definition: To include or place someone among a group.
senses.usage_conditions: Especially used with مَعَ in the Quranic construction “include us among …,” rather than meaning physical writing.

senses.definition: To enter into a written contract of emancipation with someone.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction concerns a contract between an enslaved person and the master, under which payment leads to freedom; the act is reciprocal between the parties.

senses.definition: To have a text written for oneself; to procure or fabricate a written account.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic accusation, the subject is said to have had earlier tales written or transcribed for him, rather than necessarily writing them personally.

senses.definition: A writer, scribe, secretary, or recorder.
senses.usage_conditions: The active participle can denote a person engaged in writing or recording, including scribes and recorders.
An older lexical extension associates literacy with learning; this use is explicitly connected with Quranic expressions involving كَاتِبٌ.

senses.definition: A written text, document, book, record, register, or letter.
senses.usage_conditions: Denotes a physical or conceived written object, including a written communication and a record of information or deeds.

senses.definition: A revealed scripture or divinely given book.
senses.usage_conditions: Can refer to a revealed scripture such as the Torah, Gospel, or Quran, and to the authoritative contents conveyed by such a scripture.

senses.definition: A divine prescription, ordinance, judgment, decree, or appointed destiny.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for a ruling or determination established by God, including an obligatory ordinance, a prescribed term, and a decree governing events.

senses.definition: A divinely grounded proof or authoritative warrant.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic argumentation, كتاب may denote an established warrant from God rather than merely the physical document containing it.
A passive participle describing something whose mention or description has been set down in writing or otherwise recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To judge, pass sentence, or decree against someone that he should do something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction كَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ كَذَا, especially of a judgment or sentence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw together, bring together, or conjoin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general classical branch of the root’s joining sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To close the vulva of a camel or mule with a ring or thong.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The device conjoins the edges to prevent mating.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sew or bind a waterskin or similar leather receptacle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May mean sewing it with two thongs or binding its mouth so that its contents do not escape.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a she-camel accept a young animal that is not her own.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The described practice involves a device at the nostrils to prevent the camel from detecting the young animal’s smell.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect a military unit or troop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical usage related to assembling a كَتِيبَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To tie or bind the udder of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived Form II usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prepare or arrange troops in ordered units.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II military usage, especially arranging forces troop by troop.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Correspondence or writing to one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derived noun can denote reciprocal written communication between two people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dictate something for another person to write.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV causative construction, as in dictating an ode or other text.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To teach the art of writing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV causative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gird oneself and draw one’s garments together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical Form V usage involving gathering clothing around the body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect itself into a group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an army or other organized body assembling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To write or transcribe a book from another book.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII nominal and verbal branch concerning copying or transcription.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To register one’s name in an official list.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of enrollment among recipients of stipends or maintenance and of registration in a military roster.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To request or have a book or similar text written for oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Distinct from personally transcribing a text; the construction presents the subject as procuring its writing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become obstructed bodily, with urine suppressed or the belly constipated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical medical usage of Form VIII.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask someone to write something for oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X request construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thong used for sewing a waterskin or leather receptacle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun for the sewing or binding thong.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A device used to close the vulva of a camel or mule.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A ring or similar thong used to prevent the female animal from being covered.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seam, suture, or thong-joined stitch in a skin or hide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to the joined place where a thong brings two surfaces or edges together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mode or manner of writing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal usage distinct from the concrete sewing sense of كُتْبَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bookseller.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A vulgar or nonstandard designation; the regular form would be كتابيّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A receptacle for ink.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun homonymous with the ordinary noun for a book or written document.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A skin sewn with two thongs or bound closed at its mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing a leather receptacle whose opening has been secured.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The art or practice of writing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun used as the name of the writing skill.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An army, military force, corps, or troop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May denote a collected portion of an army, including a troop of horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small round-headed arrow used by boys in learning to shoot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete technical noun, with variant lexical discussion in the source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A school or place where writing is taught.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is disputed in the source, which also records an interpretation referring to the boys of a school rather than the place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A teacher of the art of writing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active occupational noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female mule whose vulva has been closed with a ring or thong.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized passive-participial usage concerning prevention of mating.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bunch of grapes or similar cluster from which part has been eaten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized derived adjective or noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Swollen or full.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The ceremony of a marriage contract.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A legal or customary usage referring to performance of the contract, not to the certificate itself.

cautions: Lane’s historical Quran citation notation is used only as lexical evidence; modern verse locations in the examples come from the supplied QAC occurrences.
The Form III Quran occurrence is an inflected imperative; the public headword is normalized to the Classical Arabic perfect citation form كَاتَبَ.
The possessive form كتابي is accounted for under the core noun كتاب rather than displayed as a separate lexical headword.
